concept.title: What Makes a Password Strong?
concept.shortdesc: Strong passwords rely on length, randomness, and uniqueness—rather than complex symbols—to protect your accounts from data breaches and phishing attacks.

conbody.p: Cybercriminals commonly steal passwords through phishing websites or obtain password databases from data breaches. If you reuse the same password across multiple accounts, a breach on a single external website puts both your university and personal accounts at risk.

section.title: Characteristics of a Strong Password
section.p: Per the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), length is the most critical factor in password strength, taking priority over mandatory special characters or numbers. Effective password security relies on four core practices:

ul.li: Prioritize length: Use passwords of at least 15 characters to dramatically increase resistance to automated cracking.
Use memorable passphrases: Combine multiple unrelated words into a 15- to 18-character phrase that is easy for you to remember but hard for attackers to guess.
Keep every password unique: Never reuse passwords across different websites or services so a single breach cannot compromise multiple accounts.
Add extra authentication layers: Pair strong passwords with multi-factor authentication (MFA) or phishing-resistant passkeys for the strongest defense.
